extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and review-form criteria for evaluating submissions to the AISTATS 2024 conference, including how to score theory, experiments, novelty, clarity, reproducibility, ethics, and overall recommendation. Also contains best practices and procedural instructions for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper and its contributions; summarize the paper motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph. Provide 3 keywords about the paper’s topic and 3 keywords about your research expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable to ACs and chairs; helps identify misunderstandings. Contributions that warrant publication can be theoretical, methodological, algorithmic, empirical, bridge papers, or critical analyses. Use the keyword questions to detect expertise mismatch and consider lowering confidence if mismatch is noticed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of theory and theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether theoretical claims and theorems are correct, contain minor errors, or contain major errors/trivial results (options: Correct; Minor errors; Major errors or trivial results; Not applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If marking minor/major errors, specify details. Incorrect claims or methodology are primary reasons for rejection. Provide detailed, specific, polite comments with references when relevant. Example comments provided for major/ minor errors (e.g., pointing out missing factors or incorrect complexity). If assumptions are unrealistic relative to literature, comment (and justify) in additional comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of empirical results
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate empirical significance (options: Significant with well supported statistical metrics and appropriate baselines; Mixed results; Generally not significant; Not applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If results are mixed or not significant, specify concerns (max 1000 characters). Comments should be detailed and point out missing baselines or other issues; example explains when a missing baseline undermines significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of theoretical results and/or empirical methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge novelty (options: Ground-breaking new results; New results significantly different; New but incremental/combinatorial; Known results or trivial extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incremental or known, cite previous publications that support this view (max 1000 characters). Consider how the contribution may be used/influential; solid technical papers exploring new directions are preferred over incremental advances. Do not use generic criteria like 'area is important' or 'well-written' as substitutes for novelty evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of non-conventional contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the submission contains non-conventional contributions such as out-of-the-box ideas, new problems/tasks, or bridging-fields work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that novel/interdisciplinary works may be easy to criticize; avoid dismissive criticism and account for bias against not-yet-widely-accepted assumptions or models. Comment on non-conventional aspects of assumptions, model design, and methods when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the paper is clearly written and well organized, including whether it clearly states contributions, notation, results, explains theoretical assumptions, and motivates methodology with examples where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not clear, make constructive suggestions for improvement. A well-written paper should provide enough information for an expert reader to reproduce results. Provide concrete, specific feedback rather than vague complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how clearly the submission discusses how it differs from or relates to prior work, and whether important related works or baselines are missing or described incorrectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible assessments: All related works clearly discussed; All related works cited but discussion less clear; Missing some related works (minor); Some important works/baselines missing or described incorrectly. Explain in additional comments whether submission is written with due scholarship. Authors are not expected to cite very recent preprints (<4 months before submission deadline) in detail; such works are considered concurrent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional comments (feedback and suggestions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional field for additional comments, suggestions for improvement, questions for authors, and what the reviewer would do differently to improve the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague or dismissive complaints; be constructive and help authors understand your viewpoint. Remember you're assessing scientific contribution, not your personal interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether there are enough details to reproduce the main experimental results (options: Sufficient details; Some amount of details; Not enough; Not applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether assumptions, experimental settings, and limitations are clearly stated in paper and supplementary material. If information is insufficient, list this as a weakness in additional comments. Looking at supplementary material is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper score (overall recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall paper score (Reject; Borderline reject; Borderline accept; Accept; Top 10% of accepted papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall score should reflect your assessment of the submission’s contributions; do NOT adjust scores to match perceived conference acceptance rates or because your assigned set is unrepresentative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate reviewer confidence in their assessment (options range from 'Educated guess' to 'Absolutely certain').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose based on familiarity with topic and whether math/details were carefully checked. Compare your keywords for expertise vs paper keywords; low match suggests lower confidence. Use 'Absolutely certain' sparingly and only when proofs/experiments and related work have been carefully checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns / societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the submission raises potential ethical concerns or negative societal impacts (No concern; Minor concerns; Major concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper discusses potential negative societal impact/ethical issues; if absent but relevant, recommend including such discussion. This ethics rating should be independent from the overall paper score; flag papers that may need additional ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer must agree to abide by the AISTATS Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to AISTATS Code of Conduct. This is a required commitment for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must keep papers, supplementary materials, code and reviews confidential and delete submitted code at the end of the review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not divulge author identities if discovered. Confidentiality includes not sharing files and deleting code after the cycle to comply with confidentiality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to Area Chair
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional confidential field for comments to the Area Chair (e.g., comparisons to other submissions, minor formatting issues, blunt criticisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for material you do not want authors to see. If you accidentally learn author identities, do not reveal them. Confidential comments can include explicit comparisons and blunt wording not suitable for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for reviewer conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on tone and conduct: Be thoughtful, be fair, be useful, be specific, be flexible, be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid crushing early-career authors' spirits; do not let personal feelings affect reviews; produce useful reviews for authors/other reviewers/ACs; avoid vague statements; be open to revising your review after discussion; respect deadlines and notify Area Chair if you cannot complete on time. If pressured to change a review, notify Program Chairs; report unethical behavior to Area Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling minor formatting issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor formatting problems (e.g., inconsistent citation styles) should not be desk-rejected and should not change your score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag formatting issues but do not change evaluation score because of them. Conference staff will ensure style is correct for accepted papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material may be included in the same PDF or separately; reviewers may treat extra pages as supplementary materials and looking at supplementary material is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors forgot to split supplementary pages from the main paper, treat these extra pages as supplementary. Use discretion; consulting supplementary material is optional for evaluating the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: External links and code handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance about external links (e.g., URLs to code) and anonymous GitHub: reviewers are discouraged from following external links; reviewing supplementary code is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not follow external links unless willing to accept safety and de-anonymization risks. If accessing anonymous GitHub, download or clone after logging out of your own GitHub account; do not fork repositories (may reveal identity). Submitted code may contain security vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to access assigned papers (procedural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for accessing assigned papers via the CMT portal: login with reviewer CMT email, select 'Reviewer' role, download assigned submissions via 'Actions -> Download Files'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reminds reviewers that reviewing is double-blind so author information will not be visible in the system.
